step1_figure.circuit_type: PMOS current mirror biased with an ideal current source
step1_figure.description: Figure 20.11a shows a PMOS current mirror (M1 and M2) where the diode-connected PMOS M1 is biased with an ideal 10 uA reference current source to eliminate supply dependence from the reference path, while M2 mirrors this current to ground. The circuit is also used in Section 20.1.5 (Fig. 20.25 on page 631) to evaluate the temperature dependence of the PMOS gate-to-source reference voltage.

vsg_nominal.description: Gate-to-source voltage of diode-connected PMOS transistor M1 at nominal conditions (VDD=1.8V, T=27°C)

equation.explanation: Square-law saturation characteristic relating reference drain current IREF to the gate-to-source bias voltage of M1.
equation.assumptions: Long-channel square law saturation, negligible channel-length modulation for initial estimate

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by threshold voltage |V_THP| (0.42V) plus the PMOS overdrive voltage (~0.2V) required to conduct 10 uA.

output_current.description: Output current Io mirrored through M2 at nominal VDD = 1.8V and Vout = 0V

equation.formula: I_o = I_REF * (1 + lambda * V_SD2) / (1 + lambda * V_SD1)
equation.explanation: Calculates mirrored output current accounting for drain-to-source voltage mismatch between M1 and M2.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are identical geometries operating in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Since V_SD2 (1.8V) is larger than V_SD1 (0.62V), channel-length modulation increases Io above IREF.

current_ratio.description: Current mirroring ratio Io / IREF reflecting channel-length modulation mismatch

equation.formula: I_o / I_REF = (1 + lambda * V_SD2) / (1 + lambda * V_SD1)
equation.explanation: Ratio of output current to reference current as dictated by channel length modulation.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are matched in size and temperature.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite output resistance of M2 causes a systematic current gain of ~11% when M2 drain is tied to ground.

supply_sensitivity.description: Sensitivity of the mirrored output current Io to supply voltage variations dIo/dVDD

equation.explanation: Because IREF is an ideal current source, VSG1 remains constant with VDD; therefore, changes in VDD only modulate VSD2 of M2.
equation.assumptions: Ideal reference current source; PMOS operates in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Unlike resistor biasing, the ideal current source dramatically lowers supply sensitivity to less than 1 uA/V.

temp_coeff_vsg.description: Temperature coefficient of the PMOS gate-to-source reference voltage dVSG/dT

equation.explanation: The change in diode-connected PMOS gate-source voltage with temperature is dominated by the threshold voltage temperature coefficient.
equation.assumptions: Constant reference current IREF over temperature.

sky130_expected.calculation: From Chapter 9 (Fig. 9.30b) and Section 20.1.5 (Fig. 20.25), PMOS |V_THP| decreases with temperature at approximately -0.6 mV/°C. Hence dV_SG/dT = -0.6 mV/°C = -6.0e-4 V/°C.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker explicitly measures and states on page 631 that VSG varies at a rate of -0.6 mV/°C.

temp_coeff_io.description: Temperature coefficient of mirrored output current dIo/dT

equation.explanation: If IREF is ideal and constant with temperature, both matched MOSFETs drift together, keeping Io essentially independent of temperature except for second-order channel-length modulation changes.
equation.assumptions: M1 and M2 are at identical temperature.

sky130_expected.reasoning: As stated in Section 20.1.5, when IREF is independent of temperature, the mirrored current is also virtually independent of temperature.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for the PMOS current mirror measuring nominal OP bias points, VDD supply sensitivity via DC sweep (Fig. 20.11b), and temperature coefficients of VSG and Io (Fig. 20.25).
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Baker Fig. 20.11a & Fig. 20.25 PMOS Current Mirror
.param W_xm1=10u L_xm1=1u
.param W_xm2=10u L_xm2=1u

.lib ${SKY130_PDK} tt

* DUT
xm2 0 VD1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm1 VD1 VD1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
IREF VD1 0 10µ

.control
set filetype=ascii

* === 1. DC Operating Point Analysis (Nominal at 27C) ===
op
let i_out_op = -i(vdd) - 10e-6
let v_sg_op = 1.8 - v(vd1)
let ratio_op = i_out_op / 10e-6
print v(vd1) v_sg_op i_out_op ratio_op

* === 2. Supply Voltage Sweep (Fig. 20.11b) ===
dc VDD 1.5 2.0 0.01
let i_out_dc = -i(vdd) - 10e-6
let d_io_dvdd = deriv(i_out_dc)
meas dc io_nom find i_out_dc at=1.8
meas dc supply_sens find d_io_dvdd at=1.8
print io_nom supply_sens

* === 3. Temperature Sweep (Fig. 20.25 & Section 20.1.5) ===
dc temp 0 100 1
let v_sg_temp = 1.8 - v(vd1)
let d_vsg_dtemp = deriv(v_sg_temp)
let i_out_temp = -i(vdd) - 10e-6
let d_io_dtemp = deriv(i_out_temp)

meas dc vd1_at_27 find v(vd1) at=27
meas dc vsg_at_27 find v_sg_temp at=27
meas dc tc_vsg find d_vsg_dtemp at=27
meas dc tc_io find d_io_dtemp at=27
print vd1_at_27 vsg_at_27 tc_vsg tc_io

quit
.endc
.end
